intro_md:
**Week 1 · Lesson 6 – Weekend review: The story so far (~60 min).** No new grammar today. You meet **everything from this week again** – the people, the chunks, the linking words – in a new conversation. This is how words become automatic: **the same words, many times, in new places.**

| Part | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| ① Learn | The story so far + all Week 1 chunks in one table | 10 min |
| ② Try it | 8 mixed checks from the whole week | 6 min |
| ③ Listen | Nam tells Jess about his first week (3 rounds) | 15 min |
| ④ Listen again | Shadowing – whisper along with Nam | 10 min |
| ⑤ Look back | Your week: what is easier now? | 8 min |
| ✓ | Feedback + 📤 Submit | 3 min |

parts.title: The story so far
parts.md:
![Hope Street](data/img/w1/cover.svg)

**Hope Street, Manchester.** Nam moves into Flat 2 at number 14. **Margaret** (Flat 1) knows everything about everyone. The heating wakes him up at 3 a.m. At the **café on the corner**, **Jess** makes the best bacon sandwich in Manchester. At work, **Claire** is his manager and **Tom** talks very fast. **Mr Patel** (Flat 3) needs a hand with a new TV. Nam takes the **tram** to buy a SIM card.

### All Week 1 chunks – read them aloud once

| Chunk | Example from the story |
|---|---|
| **be / get used to + V-ing / noun** | I'm getting used to the rain. |
| **it takes + time + to V** | It takes about ten minutes. |
| **I'd better / I'd love** | I'd better go. · I'd love a coffee. |
| **How's it going? – So far so good** | – |
| **show sb around · let me know · give sb a hand** | Could you give me a hand? |
| **get the hang of sth** | It takes a while to get the hang of it. |
| **opposite · next to · on the corner** | The stop is opposite the church. |
| **get on / get off · take the tram** | Get off at Market Street. |

### Linking words – the road signs
**although / even though** (surprise) · **however / yet / though** (turn) · **rather / rather than** (not A → B) · **unless** (if not) · **in other words** (same idea again)

parts.title: Mixed checks from the whole week (not graded)

questions.q: I'm not used to ___ so early.
___ he was tired, Nam helped Mr Patel.
Take the tram ___ you want to walk for an hour.
It ___ about twenty minutes to walk to work.
*"So far so good."* means…
The phone shop is ___ the bank – right beside it.
He didn't ask Tom to repeat. ___, he smiled and nodded.
*"I'd better go."* – I'd = …

parts.title: Nam's first week
parts.md:
![Nam and Jess at the café on Saturday](data/img/w1/l6-cafe.svg)

Saturday, at the café. Jess asks Nam about his first week. Almost every chunk from this week is here – listen for them.

**Listen in 3 rounds, at normal speed – don't stop, don't translate:**
1. **No transcript** – follow the story. 2. **With the transcript** – eyes on the words while you hear them. 3. **No transcript again** – notice how much more you hear.

listen.text: So, Nam, you've survived your first week! How was it?
Honestly? Tiring, but much better than I expected. I'm getting used to the rain, at least.
Ha! And work? Do you like your team?
Yes, they're really friendly. Tom talks very fast, though. On Monday I understood about half of what he said. Now I understand most of it.
That's because you hear him every day. It's like music – the more you hear it, the easier it gets.
Exactly. And I found the tram, I bought a SIM card, and I helped Mr Patel carry a TV up the stairs.
Raj and his TVs! He buys a new one every year. Has Margaret invited you for tea yet?
Not yet. Although she's told me everything about everyone on this street.
She will. And when she does, say yes. Her lemon cake is the best in Manchester. Rather than buying a cake, you should just wait for an invitation!
Good advice. In other words – be patient and be hungry!

questions.q: How was Nam's first week, in his words?
Why does Nam understand Tom better now?
options: Because he hears him every day.
Because he took an English class.

questions.q: What does Mr Patel do every year?
What is Margaret famous for, according to Jess?
**Dictation:** type Nam's sentence starting with *"Not yet. Although…"*
*"In other words – be patient and be hungry!"* What advice is Nam repeating in other words?
How much of this conversation did you understand on the **first** listen/read? Write a number, e.g. 75

parts.title: Shadowing – whisper along
parts.md:
Play the conversation in part ③ again **with the transcript**. This time, **whisper Nam's lines at the same time as him** – same speed, same rhythm. Don't stop the audio. Do it twice.

This is not speaking practice – it trains your **ear** to expect the rhythm, so the words arrive faster next time.

questions.q: Which of Nam's sentences was the hardest to whisper at full speed? Copy it.
Compared with Monday, is it easier to hear *I'm, you'll, it's, I'd* now?
Did you translate into Vietnamese less this week?
Which lesson or part helped you the most this week, and why?
Week 2 theme is **Food & Eating Out**. Anything you'd like inside it? (a topic, a type of video, more/less of something)
